content.body:
The heavier Allied tanks met on the battlefield (such as the Matilda II) forced the German High Command to reconsider all of their current AFV armaments, so the StuG.IIIb was upgunned simultaneously with the longer 75mm as employed in the Pz.IV series upgrades.
Improving some of the more egregious design failings of the B, this resulted in the Stug.IIIg a very effective tank destroyer produced far more cheaply and quickly than their more complicated turreted cousins. Nearly 10,000 were ultimately produced and deployed into every theater of the war. As the tide of the conflict for the Germans turned from offensive to defensive, the ambush AFVs like the StuG.IIIg became more and more useful and preferred in production. Like the Pz.IVg, the more lethal anti-tank ability of the 75mm meant that HEAT ammunition was no longer included as standard ammo.
Control Variations: Crew 1 driver has a non-zoom view slit to his left. Crew 2 Commander may use the numpad 0 or Ins key to look through periscopes of his cupola without exposing himself outside the tank. He may not use his included rangefinder unless he unbuttons, however. Crew 3 must still deploy a sight to aim the gun, but in this case it peeks out of a small roof hole instead of opening the shot-trap view slit.
The utility of the StuG.IIIg depends a great deal on the tactical situation. If on the defensive, the StuG.IIIg is probably the best ambusher of the game ... the low profile, camouflage, and sheer lethality of the gun mean that if it gets the first shot, it usually wins. On the offensive, it is harder to use. If spotted, Allied opponents will hunt you down with great dedication. Without a turret it is often hard to get into a good firing position without completely exposing your tank.
As expected for a turretless tank, SA is a problem and the limited ammo stocks remain a serious limit on the StuGs ability to sustain a gun duel or hold a position in the face of a persistent attack. On the plus side, even if you are identified, the heavy frontal armor means good protection for withdrawal, particularly from the frontal aspect.
Lacking an defensive MG, the StuG is at the mercy of close- in enemy infantry; if you identify infantry around you, just pack up and run; if they are sappers then they may already be planting a charge on you, even if they are just regular infantry they will smoke you with smoke markers to ID you as a target or to prevent you firing when the sappers show up; and they most certainly will at some point because StuGs are hated by all those who must fight them. So do not stick around !
Note: HE rounds tend to fall shorter than AP rounds, especially at long ranges. Unlike the Pz.IVg, the StuG.IIIg does not have the two-tier range setting system in the gunsight. If you are going to be using a StuG.IIIg a lot, it is worthwhile to jump into a Pz.IVg offline and jot down some corresponding ranges for reference when shooting the StuG.IIIg 75mm gun.
